$comment: The Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable the Windows installer runs (installer-hooks.nsh), pinned by SHA-256 and staged by scripts/ci/stage-vc-redist.mjs. The url is the versioned download behind https://aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe (Microsoft's latest supported redistributable; its path carries the SHA-256), read on 2026-11-11, file and product version 14.52.37029.0 (the installer hooks' PITWALL_VC_* defines hold the same Major.Minor.Bld). To move the pin, take the new url from that redirect, download it, check that the SHA-256 in the path matches the bytes, that Windows shows a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature and the new version, then edit this file and the defines. Why the package and not app-local DLLs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/redistributing-visual-cpp-files (central deployment is recommended because Microsoft services the libraries; app-local is not recommended). Licence basis: the Visual Studio 2026 and later 'Distributable Code Files' list (REDIST.TXT, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2026/redistribution, read 2026-11-11; the 2022 list has the same wording): 'Subject to the License Terms for the software, you may copy and distribute the following files, unmodified, as a part of the installation package of your program' (Visual C++ Runtime Files, including everything under VC\redist); the same package from the Latest supported downloads page is 'limited to licensed Visual Studio users'. Pitwall ships it unmodified, inside its installer. Pitwall's third-party notices list it (apps/pitwall/docs/third-party/microsoft-vc-redist.md).
